# SwapLayer

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/SwapLayer)](https://pypi.org/project/SwapLayer/)
[![Python 3.10–3.13](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%E2%80%933.13-blue)](https://pypi.org/project/SwapLayer/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/LICENSE)

**One Python interface for billing, email, SMS, storage, identity, and
verification providers, with Django and FastAPI integrations.**

Part of the [Tunet](https://www.tunet.xyz/engineering/) open-source libraries, alongside [AccessGate](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/access_gate), [GeoCanon](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/geo_canon), and [SessionArmor](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/session_armor). See the [SwapLayer product page](https://www.tunet.xyz/engineering/swap-layer/) for the public capability overview.

SwapLayer provides Python interfaces for billing, email, SMS, storage, and
identity integrations. Configure the services you use, then call their adapters
through `get_provider()`. Django supplies email, OAuth, model, and admin
integrations; a small FastAPI adapter attaches configuration to application
state.

## Features

| Service | Selectable provider values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | `django`, `smtp` | SendGrid, Mailgun, SES, and similar services use Django's Anymail backend settings. |
| `billing` | `stripe`, `paypal`, `square` | Capabilities differ; see the billing guide. |
| `sms` | `twilio`, `sns` | SNS history, delivery lookup, and balance are limited placeholders. |
| `storage` | `local`, `django`, `gcs` | S3/Azure use `django` with a configured Django storage backend. |
| `identity` | `workos`, `auth0` | Django OAuth integration; use the documented app registry. |
| `verification` | `stripe` | Stripe Identity; other verification providers are not implemented. |

Structured settings use `billing`, `communications.email`, `communications.sms`,
`storage`, `identity`, and `verification`. In plain Python call
`configure(...)`. In Django assign a `SwapLayerSettings` instance or dictionary
to `SWAPLAYER`. Environment configuration uses complete paths such as
`SWAPLAYER_BILLING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` or
`SWAPLAYER_IDENTITY_WORKOS_APPS_DEFAULT_API_KEY`. A misspelt `SWAPLAYER_`
variable or an unknown settings key fails validation.

## Version 1.0

The 1.x compatibility promise covers documented configuration, factory names,
adapter method names, and normalized result fields. Underscore-prefixed
helpers, vendor SDK objects, and historical development notes are outside that
promise. Vendor behavior and access policies remain governed by the provider.
Python 3.10–3.13 is tested, and the Django integrations support Django 4.2–6.x
(`Django<7`).

SwapLayer 1.0.0 is tagged (`v1.0.0`) but not yet published to PyPI, which still
serves 0.3.0. The tag predates the changes listed under Unreleased in the
changelog, so until the next release is published, install from `main`, adding
extras as needed:

```bash
pip install "SwapLayer @ git+https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer@main"
pip install "SwapLayer[stripe] @ git+https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer@main"
```

Upgrading from 0.x: replace root `email`/`sms` settings with `communications`;
use `send_email`, `send_sms`, and the storage adapter's
`upload_file`/`get_file_url`/`file_exists` methods. Django storage `list_files`
now returns a list of object dictionaries; `list_directory` preserves the former
directory shape. WorkOS common list methods return object lists; `*_page`
methods expose cursor envelopes. Stripe-specific payment/checkout options are
keyword arguments after the common positional idempotency key. PayPal now
handles zero-decimal HUF/JPY/TWD without dividing by 100; review
provider-specific amount conventions when migrating. Tenant scopes must contain
`{organization_id}` and reject unsafe paths; omitted contexts no longer grant
system access. Django app labels are `swap_layer_<area>` (for example
`swap_layer_billing`), a WorkOS `cookie_password` must be a Fernet key, and the
MCP tools have new names. See the [changelog](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Installation

Core dependencies are Pydantic 2, Requests, and Tenacity.

```bash
pip install SwapLayer
pip install "SwapLayer[stripe]"     # Stripe 16.x
pip install "SwapLayer[email]"      # Django and django-anymail
pip install "SwapLayer[sms]"        # Twilio 9.x; add [aws] for SNS
pip install "SwapLayer[gcs]"        # Native Google Cloud Storage
pip install "SwapLayer[identity]"   # Django, WorkOS 10.x, Authlib
pip install "SwapLayer[mcp]"        # MCP SDK 1.x, for create_mcp_server()
```

Other extras: `django`, `fastapi`, `paypal`, `square`, `aws`, `azure`, `all`,
and `dev`. PayPal and Square use the core HTTP dependencies. Email and OAuth
require configured Django settings; storage, billing, Stripe Identity, and
Twilio support explicit configuration without Django.

## Quick start

```python
from io import BytesIO
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider

configure(storage={"provider": "local", "media_root": "./media", "media_url": "/media/"})
storage = get_provider("storage")
storage.upload_file("documents/hello.txt", BytesIO(b"hello"))
assert storage.download_file("documents/hello.txt") == b"hello"
assert storage.file_exists("documents/hello.txt")
print(storage.get_file_url("documents/hello.txt"))
```

Local URLs are plain paths; the library does not serve files or enforce URL
expiry. Applications must control access to private files. Keep the local
storage directory writable only by trusted application processes.

## Tenant-scoped storage

For tenant boundaries, use an explicit verified identity context:

```python
from swap_layer.storage.security import StorageSecurityContext, storage_context

context = StorageSecurityContext(
    organization_id="org-123", user_id="user-456", role="member",
    scope_format="tenants/{organization_id}",
)
with storage_context(storage, context) as scoped:
    scoped.upload_from_string("hello.txt", "tenant data")
```

This produces `tenants/org-123/hello.txt`. Contexts consume identity already
verified by your application; they do not verify JWTs. A context's permissions
come from its role (`admin`, `manager`, `member`, or `viewer`) or an explicit
permission set; a context with neither has none. Unscoped access needs
`StorageSecurityContext.system_context(reason=...)`.

## Billing

```python
import os
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider

configure(billing={"provider": "stripe", "stripe": {
    "secret_key": os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"],
    "webhook_secret": os.environ.get("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),
}})
billing = get_provider("billing")
# Uses your provider account; run against a test account first.
customer = billing.create_customer(email="customer@example.com")
```

Pass integer provider minor currency units, represented by `Decimal` where
required by the adapter, to payment amounts; a fraction of a minor unit raises
`PaymentValidationError`. Provider IDs, tax rules, recurring billing, and
capability differences require application review. Stripe exposes the broadest
catalog, usage-meter, Entitlements, and webhook administration surface.

## MCP server

SwapLayer includes a local stdio MCP server; `pip install SwapLayer` is enough:

```bash
swaplayer-mcp
```

`python -m swap_layer.mcp` starts the same server. From a source checkout, run
`python mcp/server.py`. It serves SwapLayer's public agent contract and
packaged guides (resources under `opensource://swap_layer/`, 17 tools, and 4
prompts) and reads the caller's `SWAPLAYER_` environment configuration. Most
tools return guidance or example code. `send_test_email`, `send_test_sms`, and
`check_storage` with `testUpload` use the caller's own provider credentials and
can cause provider charges or file changes, so clients must obtain approval
before those calls. The package includes no hosted agent service, shared
provider account, or owner credential. Install `SwapLayer[mcp]` only to embed
the server with the MCP SDK through `swap_layer.mcp.create_mcp_server()`. See
[docs/mcp.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/mcp.md) and
[mcp/README.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/mcp/README.md) for the tools, methods, and limits.

## Scope and limitations

Provider capabilities differ. Moving a provider can require data migration,
webhook changes, and application changes. Unsupported operations raise errors
or have documented limitations.

Tests use mocked provider calls, plus installed-package and Django admin
checks. They do not establish live provider certification, and SwapLayer has
not had an independent security audit; the
[security assurance case](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md) lists the evidence the
repository provides.

## Documentation

- [Documentation index](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/README.md): guides, security
  documents, and the release procedure.
- Guides: [billing](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/billing.md), [email](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/email.md), [SMS](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/sms.md), [storage](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/storage.md), [identity](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/identity-platform.md), [verification](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/identity-verification.md), [architecture](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), [MCP tools](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/mcp.md).
- Security: [security policy](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/SECURITY.md),
  [threat model](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md),
  [security assurance](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md),
  [audit scope](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/AUDIT_SCOPE.md), and
  [secure development](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURE_DEVELOPMENT.md).
- [Changelog](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), including which versions reached PyPI.

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer.git
cd swap_layer
python -m pip install -e ".[all,dev]"
python -m ruff check src tests
python -m mypy src/swap_layer
python -m bandit -r src
python -m pytest --cov=swap_layer --cov-branch
```

These are the checks the manual CI workflows run. The
[security assurance case](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md) lists the full
evidence commands, including the dependency audit.

After editing README.md, SECURITY.md, or a docs guide, run
`python tools/sync_mcp_guidance.py`: the MCP server serves packaged copies of
them, and `tests/test_mcp_guidance.py` fails until those copies match.

## Contributing and releases

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the owner-reviewed contribution
process and [VERSIONING.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/VERSIONING.md) for the shared SemVer and
release policy. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in
[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/SECURITY.md). CI workflows run only when the owner
starts them, so include your local test results in pull requests. Everyone
taking part follows the [code of conduct](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

# Architecture

`swap_layer.configure` stores process-local validated settings. `get_provider(service)` selects adapters for `email`, `billing` (`payments` is still accepted), `sms`, `storage`, `identity`, or `verification`. Factories import optional providers when requested. Core imports do not configure Django or require every optional SDK.

Configuration groups are `billing`, `communications.email`, `communications.sms`, `storage`, `identity`, and `verification`. Plain Python can configure supported standalone adapters explicitly. Django loads `SWAPLAYER` or legacy settings; email and OAuth use Django facilities, and the Django apps carry `swap_layer_<area>` labels such as `swap_layer_billing`. With `swap_layer` in `INSTALLED_APPS`, `python manage.py swaplayer_check` validates the configuration (`--module billing` checks one area, and `--verbose` shows the settings with every non-public value masked); `swap_layer.billing` adds `swaplayer_migrate_billing_provider`, described in the [billing guide](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/billing.md#moving-customers-to-another-provider). The FastAPI adapter stores configuration on application state and does not supply authentication, routes or middleware.

Adapters expose common method signatures and normalized results. They do not erase vendor differences. Vendor SDK objects, provider-specific extensions, dashboard state, customer IDs, webhooks and feature availability require application review. Unsupported operations must remain explicit.

Storage contexts consume trusted identity, check permissions, prefix object keys and audit operations. Applications verify identity, choose organizations and keep storage credentials/ACLs private. Local filesystem checks assume trusted OS writers and do not replace an OS sandbox.

The MCP server (`swaplayer-mcp`) is a caller-owned stdio process that serves the public agent contract, the packaged guides, configuration inspection and approved test operations. It does not connect users to the owner's agents or accounts. Public contribution text is untrusted and cannot authorize paid work, credentials, merges or publishing.

Applications own concrete Django models/migrations, callback URLs and session checks, provider account policies, queueing, retry/idempotency design, privacy retention and end-user authorization. Keep those controls at the application boundary; do not infer authorization from normalized provider data.

See the current [module guides](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/README.md), [security policy](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/SECURITY.md), and [release standards](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/VERSIONING.md). Older implementation notes describe previous designs and planned features rather than the 1.0 compatibility contract.

# Billing

Use `get_provider("billing")` (`"payments"` is still accepted) with `billing.provider` set to `stripe`, `paypal`, or `square`. The modules are under `swap_layer.billing`, including customers, subscriptions, payment intents, products and provider implementations. Changing providers requires application and data review.

## Configure

```python
import os
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider
configure(billing={"provider":"stripe", "stripe":{
    "secret_key": os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"],
    "webhook_secret": os.environ.get("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),
}})
billing = get_provider("billing")
```

Install `SwapLayer[stripe]` for Stripe 16.x. PayPal and Square use the core Requests dependency. In Django, use the same structure as `SWAPLAYER` or a `SwapLayerSettings` instance. Legacy `PAYMENT_PROVIDER` and provider key settings remain supported.

PayPal configuration is `billing={'provider':'paypal','paypal':{'client_id':...,'client_secret':...,'webhook_id':...,'sandbox':True}}`. Square uses `billing={'provider':'square','square':{'access_token':...,'location_id':...,'webhook_signature_key':...,'webhook_notification_url':...,'sandbox':True}}`. Read credentials from the caller's environment. A test label does not switch credentials to sandbox mode automatically.

## Capability boundaries

| Surface | Stripe | PayPal / Square |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customers, payments, products, prices, subscriptions, checkout, invoices, refunds | Provider adapter operations | Provider-specific mappings and limitations |
| Metered billing, promotion codes, tax-rate objects, hosted billing portal | Broad Stripe surface | Unsupported Stripe-specific operations raise validation errors |
| Entitlements and catalog discovery | Stripe-specific extensions | No equivalent common guarantee |
| Webhook verification | Stripe signature and endpoint secret | PayPal verification API with the `PAYPAL-*` headers; Square signature (with the notification URL) and a signed `created_at` |

PayPal `verify_webhook_signature(payload, signature, headers=request.headers)` reads `PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO`, `PAYPAL-CERT-URL`, `PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID`, `PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG` and `PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME` from the request headers (Django's `request.headers` or `request.META`), using `signature` as the transmission signature when the headers lack it; a missing header raises, and `payload` may be bytes or text. It requires a `webhook_id` (configured, or passed as `webhook_secret`) and fails closed: any verification status other than `SUCCESS` raises.

Square `verify_webhook_signature` rejects a missing or malformed signature as invalid, and also needs the event's signed `created_at`: at most 25 hours old (Square retries deliveries for 24 hours) and at most 5 minutes in the future. Construct `SquarePaymentProvider(..., webhook_max_age=None)` to turn the age check off. Keep processed `event_id` values for at least 25 hours and pass them to `dispatch_webhook_event(event, handlers, processed_event_ids=...)`.

PayPal has no customer object: the customer methods manage a local handle, `paypal:<email>`, which `create_subscription` uses as the subscriber. Their results carry `"local_only": True`, and remote PayPal payer IDs cannot be updated or deleted through them. PayPal's `create_billing_portal_session` raises `PaymentValidationError`: PayPal has no hosted billing portal.

Normalized objects include provider IDs and status fields; IDs cannot be moved between accounts/vendors by changing configuration. Some provider-specific invoice/customer operations are partial mappings. Test the exact operations your application needs in a non-production account; mocked unit tests are not live account certification.

## Amounts and idempotency

Use finite integer **provider minor units**, represented by `Decimal` where the interface requires it. `Decimal("1234")` is GBP 12.34. PayPal treats HUF, JPY and TWD as zero-decimal currencies, so `Decimal("1234")` means 1234 units there. HUF/TWD rules can differ across vendors: review amount conversion during provider migration. A fraction of a minor unit raises `PaymentValidationError` with every provider rather than being rounded or truncated, and PayPal also rejects malformed response precision. Every provider also rejects amounts of more than 18 digits or 64 characters. For a PayPal value string, which is in major units, the 18 digits count minor units: `"9999999999999999.99"` is the largest USD value. Raw money strings are outside the common numeric amount convention: PayPal reads them as major-unit values, and Stripe and Square read an integral string as minor units.

[PayPal's currency rules](https://developer.paypal.com/api/codes/currency/) define its zero-decimal behavior. Each provider controls supported currencies, account restrictions and API limits.

```python
from decimal import Decimal
intent = billing.create_payment_intent(
    amount=Decimal("1000"), currency="gbp",
    idempotency_key="your-application-defined-unique-operation-id",
)
```

Use stable, unique operation keys according to the provider's idempotency rules. Stripe payment/checkout methods keep the common positional idempotency argument; Stripe-specific options are keyword-only after it. Applications own retries, reconciliation, user authorization and duplicate-event tracking.

## Stripe catalog and webhooks

The Stripe adapter exposes `discover_catalog`, auto-paginated catalog helpers, mutable `update_price`, and explicit `replace_price` for immutable monetary/recurrence changes. Replacement transfers a lookup key; existing subscriptions and prior prices need explicit application migration/archival decisions. Entitlements feature/product attachment methods are provider-specific.

Webhook endpoint create/read/update/delete operations are explicit. The signing secret is returned only when created; discovery/read/update output omits it. Secure that one-time value yourself. Verify incoming signatures against raw request bytes, authorize event processing, and maintain durable idempotency/audit state. In-memory processed-event sets are not a distributed transaction store.

## Moving customers to another provider

`python manage.py swaplayer_migrate_billing_provider <from> <to>` creates each customer again in the target provider and stores the new customer ID on your model. Add `swap_layer.billing` to `INSTALLED_APPS`, and give the model the `payment_provider` and `payment_customer_id` fields of `swap_layer.billing.models.PaymentProviderCustomerMixin`.

```bash
python manage.py swaplayer_migrate_billing_provider stripe paypal --dry-run
python manage.py swaplayer_migrate_billing_provider stripe paypal --confirm
python manage.py swaplayer_migrate_billing_provider stripe paypal --confirm --model accounts.Customer
```

- Configure both providers. The target is built from its own block next to the active one (for example `SWAPLAYER["billing"]["paypal"]` while `billing.provider` stays `stripe`), or else from its legacy Django settings; an unknown or unconfigured target stops the command with an error.
- Exactly one of `--dry-run` and `--confirm` is required. Run `--dry-run` first: it lists the customers it would move and changes nothing.
- `--model app.Model` names the model that holds the customers (default `auth.User`); the command reads its `email` and its `name` or `username`.
- Only customers move: subscriptions, payment methods and invoices are not migrated. Each new customer records `migrated_from` and `old_customer_id` in its metadata, and a customer that fails is reported while the rest continue.
- `migrate_payment_provider` is a deprecated alias through 1.x: it prints a deprecation notice and runs the new command.

`get_payment_provider("paypal")` (from `swap_layer`, also `swap_layer.billing.get_provider`) builds a named provider the same way, without changing the configured one.

Applications own customer data, concrete Django models/migrations, payment authorization, refund approval, regulatory obligations and provider accounts. Runtime MCP does not execute production payment transactions; generated examples are text requiring application review.

# Email

Email adapters require configured Django settings. Install `SwapLayer[email]` for Django and Anymail, or `SwapLayer[django]` for Django's built-in backends.

The selectable values are `django` and `smtp`. SendGrid, Mailgun, SES and other Anymail services are Django backend choices, not SwapLayer provider values.

```python
# Django settings.py
import os
SWAPLAYER = {"communications": {"email": {"provider": "django"}}}
EMAIL_BACKEND = "anymail.backends.sendgrid.EmailBackend"
ANYMAIL = {"SENDGRID_API_KEY": os.environ["SENDGRID_API_KEY"]}
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL = "sender@example.com"
```

```python
from swap_layer import get_provider
email = get_provider("email")
result = email.send_email(
    to=["recipient@example.com"], subject="Hello", text_body="Example message",
    reply_to=["support@example.com"],
)
```

For local testing use `EMAIL_BACKEND = 'django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend'`. The `smtp` provider (`communications.email.provider='smtp'`) sends through Django's configured `EMAIL_BACKEND`; with Django's default SMTP backend, Django reads `EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_PORT`, TLS and account settings. When neither `EMAIL_TIMEOUT` nor the mailer's `timeout` option is set, SwapLayer gives the SMTP connection a 30-second timeout.

Use `send_email`, `send_template_email`, and `send_bulk_email` as implemented by your adapter. Django adapter templates are Django template paths rendered by the application. `metadata` passed to a send goes to Anymail's message `metadata` and `tags` (a `tags` string is one tag), never into message headers. The `django` provider returns Anymail's message ID, a sorted list when the service returns one per recipient, or `sent-via-django` when the backend reports none. `validate_webhook_signature` returns `False` for the `django` and `smtp` providers, which have no signed webhooks of their own. Rich provider analytics, suppression management, verification and webhook support are not portable guarantees; inspect the selected adapter and use vendor-specific facilities where needed. The library does not implement consent, deliverability, queueing, or account authorization policies.

Abstract models/admin helpers are under `swap_layer.communications.email.models` and `.admin`. Applications own their concrete models and migrations. Sending uses the caller's account and may incur charges; MCP test sends require explicit client approval.

# SMS

Twilio and AWS SNS are implemented. Vonage and other SMS vendors are not selectable providers. Install `SwapLayer[sms]` for Twilio 9.x or `SwapLayer[aws]` for SNS.

```python
import os
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider
configure(communications={"sms": {"provider": "twilio", "twilio": {
    "account_sid": os.environ["TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"],
    "auth_token": os.environ["TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"],
    "from_number": os.environ["TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER"],
}}})
result = get_provider("sms").send_sms(to="+15555551234", message="Example")
```

Explicit Twilio configuration works without Django. Twilio requests time out after 30 seconds; pass `timeout=` to `TwilioSMSProvider` to change it. Use E.164 phone numbers and a test account/approved recipient before enabling real sends.

For SNS, configure `communications.sms={'provider':'sns','sns':{'region_name':'eu-west-2','sender_id':'Example'}}`. Credentials may be supplied through `aws_access_key_id`/`aws_secret_access_key` or boto3's normal IAM credential chain. The library does not supply an AWS account.

`send_sms` and `send_bulk_sms` use the selected adapter. Twilio also supplies message status/history and lookup/account operations; its `opt_out_number` and `opt_in_number` return the status `not_supported` and do not call Twilio, which applies STOP and START replies itself. SNS delivery-status lookup returns `unknown`, message history returns an empty list, and balance is unavailable; those are documented placeholders rather than live monitoring. SNS opt-out queries and opt-in calls use AWS APIs. Phone validation is provider-dependent (SNS validates with the provider's own AWS settings) and is not proof of ownership.

Applications implement messaging consent, opt-out policy, rate limits, OTP verification, and abuse controls. A provider change does not migrate phone numbers or suppression lists. Calls can incur charges against the caller's account. MCP test sends require client approval.

Django model/admin helpers are in `swap_layer.communications.sms.models` and `.admin` and require your application's concrete models and migrations.

# Storage

Select `local`, `gcs`, or `django`. Direct S3 and Azure adapter classes are not exposed; use Django's configured storage backend for those services.

```python
from io import BytesIO
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider

configure(storage={"provider": "local", "media_root": "./media"})
storage = get_provider("storage")
storage.upload_file("docs/example.txt", BytesIO(b"example"))
contents = storage.download_file("docs/example.txt")
objects = storage.list_files(prefix="docs/", max_results=100)
url = storage.get_file_url("docs/example.txt")
```

Common operations: `upload_file`, `download_file`, `delete_file`, `delete_files`, `file_exists`, `get_file_metadata`, `list_files`, `get_file_url`, `copy_file`, `move_file`, and `generate_presigned_upload_url`. Presigned uploads and expiry are backend-dependent. Local storage returns an upload placeholder and plain URLs; Django's generic adapter cannot generate presigned uploads. The application serves local URLs and enforces access control.

`list_files` returns a list of dictionaries with `file_path` and backend metadata. Django's former `{files, directories}` result is available through `list_directory`.

## Tenant boundaries

```python
from swap_layer.storage.security import StorageSecurityContext, storage_context

ctx = StorageSecurityContext(
    organization_id="org-123", user_id="user-456", role="member",
    scope_format="tenants/{organization_id}",
)
with storage_context(storage, ctx) as scoped:
    scoped.upload_from_string("report.txt", "example")
    assert scoped.download_as_text("report.txt") == "example"
```

An `admin` has every permission, including `ADMIN`; a `manager` may read, write and delete; a `member` may read and write; a `viewer` may read. A context with no role, or with a role the mapping does not know (such as `system`), has no permissions. Explicit permission sets override the role mapping. The context consumes trusted, previously verified identity; it does not verify JWTs or determine membership. Never populate it directly from unverified claims.

Non-system scopes must include `{organization_id}`. A scope may use only the plain placeholders `{organization_id}`, `{platform}` and `{role}`, without format specs or conversions, and the context must set each one it uses; otherwise building the context raises `ValueError`. `organization_id`, `platform` and `role` must each be one plain segment: letters, digits, `_` and `-`, with single dots only between them. Traversal, absolute paths, backslashes and drive/stream paths are rejected. Contexts are immutable; build a new one to change claims. System access is only through `StorageSecurityContext.system_context(reason="maintenance")`, and `StorageSecurityContext(is_system=True)` raises. Missing contexts fail closed.

`upload_file(public=True)` changes an object's access control, so it needs the `ADMIN` permission. `upload_file` and `upload_from_string` record `uploaded_by`, `organization_id` and `platform` metadata from the context, and caller metadata cannot replace them.

Local storage rejects symlinks and junctions below its configured root, including metadata sidecars. Keys must match stored names exactly, so on a case-insensitive file system `ACME/x` does not reach `acme/x`; on Windows, device names such as `CON`, `NUL` and `COM1` and segments ending in a dot or space are rejected. Local metadata keys cannot contain `:`, values must be single-line, and the sidecar files are UTF-8. The storage root and its parents must be writable only by trusted application processes: this is not an OS sandbox against concurrent filesystem replacement. `download_file(destination=...)` writes to a caller-specified local destination; validate that destination in your application. MD5 ETags are change indicators, not security checksums.

## Native GCS

Install `SwapLayer[gcs]`. Google application default credentials are supported; a credentials file is optional.

```python
configure(storage={
    "provider": "gcs", "bucket_name": "your-bucket", "project_id": "your-project",
})
```

`credentials_path`, `location`, and `storage_class` are optional settings. GCS URL signing requires credentials capable of signing. Extended bucket methods are provider-specific and are outside the common adapter surface.

## Django storage backends

Install `SwapLayer[aws]` for S3 or `SwapLayer[azure]` for Azure, configure Django's `STORAGES['default']` backend, then use `SWAPLAYER = {'storage': {'provider': 'django'}}`. Do not set the SwapLayer provider to `s3` or `azure`. Django 4.2–6.x is supported subject to each Python version's requirements. Backend ACLs, URL expiry, credentials, and serving policies remain application configuration.

Optional model/admin mixins live in `swap_layer.storage.models` and `swap_layer.storage.admin`; subclass the abstract models in your application and manage their migrations there.

# Identity integration

Install `SwapLayer[identity]`. WorkOS 10.x and Authlib integrate with Django requests and sessions; this OAuth adapter is not a standalone JWT verifier. Authenticate and authorize requests in the application before privileged provider operations.

The OAuth clients read the structured `identity` settings (`workos_apps`, `auth0_apps`, `auth0_domain`) and fall back to the legacy `WORKOS_APPS`, `AUTH0_APPS` and `AUTH0_DEVELOPER_DOMAIN` Django settings.

```python
# Django settings.py
import os
SWAPLAYER = {"identity": {"provider": "workos", "workos_apps": {"default": {
    "api_key": os.environ["WORKOS_API_KEY"],
    "client_id": os.environ["WORKOS_CLIENT_ID"],
    "cookie_password": os.environ["WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD"],  # a Fernet key
}}}}
```

`cookie_password` must be a Fernet key (32 url-safe base64-encoded bytes), which WorkOS SDK 10 uses to seal sessions; a password of another form is rejected. Generate one with:

```bash
python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```

Auth0 uses `identity={'provider': 'auth0', 'auth0_apps': {'developer': {'client_id': ..., 'client_secret': ...}}, 'auth0_domain': ...}`, or the legacy `AUTH0_APPS` and `AUTH0_DEVELOPER_DOMAIN` settings. The factory maps the default Auth0 app to `developer`. An app may also set `management_client_id` and `management_client_secret` for the Management API.

```python
from swap_layer import get_identity_client
identity = get_identity_client(app_name="default")
# Sign-in view: the client keeps the OAuth state in request.session.
# url = identity.get_authorization_url(request, redirect_uri)
# Callback view: the request's state must match one issued to this session.
# user_data = identity.exchange_code_for_user(request, code)
# identity.clear_session(request)
```

WorkOS accepts each state once, within 10 minutes of `get_authorization_url`; otherwise `exchange_code_for_user` raises `OAuthStateError` (from `swap_layer.identity.platform.adapter`). For WorkOS, `exchange_code_for_user` returns the sealed session as `sealed_session`; store it in `request.session["workos_sealed_session"]`, where `get_logout_url` reads it and `clear_session` removes it. The Auth0 client keeps its state and nonce in the session for Authlib to check. Validate callback URLs, session ownership and logout destinations at the application boundary. Follow your provider's production session guidance. Normalized user data does not grant application permissions by itself.

## Management APIs

```python
from swap_layer.identity.platform.management.factory import get_management_client
management = get_management_client()
users = management.users.list_users(per_page=20)
```

`get_management_client()` uses `identity.provider`, or the legacy `IDENTITY_PROVIDER` Django setting (default `"workos"`) when SwapLayer settings have no `identity`. WorkOS management reads its API key from `identity.workos_apps` (or the legacy `WORKOS_APPS`). Auth0 management reads `identity.auth0_apps` and `identity.auth0_domain` (or the legacy `AUTH0_APPS` and `AUTH0_DEVELOPER_DOMAIN`), with the same `default`-to-`developer` app mapping, and uses an app's `management_client_id` and `management_client_secret` when they are set, otherwise its OAuth client credentials.

Common list methods return lists of object dictionaries. WorkOS `list_users_page`, `list_organizations_page`, `list_organization_members_page`, `list_logs_page`, and `list_roles_page` expose vendor response envelopes where applicable. WorkOS uses cursor arguments (`after`/`before`); numeric pages beyond zero are explicitly unsupported. Auth0 uses page/per-page arguments.

WorkOS role creation/removal and effective-permission lookup have unsupported operations that raise `NotImplementedError`. User-specific WorkOS event queries are rejected rather than returning every user's events. Auth0 `get_stats()` returns an active-user count; daily statistics return a list. Provider APIs have different capabilities and response semantics; test migrations with a non-production tenant.

Management access uses privileged caller credentials. Keep it in owner-authorized application flows and use least privilege. It is not exposed as a production operation by the MCP server. Applications own concrete Django identity models, migrations, permission checks, PII policies and audit retention.
explain.identity-verification:
# Stripe Identity

Stripe Identity is the implemented verification provider. Persona and WorkOS verification adapters are not included. Install `SwapLayer[stripe]`; explicit configuration works without Django.

```python
import os
from swap_layer import configure, get_provider
configure(verification={
    "provider": "stripe",
    "stripe_secret_key": os.environ["STRIPE_IDENTITY_SECRET_KEY"],
    "stripe_webhook_secret": os.environ.get("STRIPE_IDENTITY_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),
})
verification = get_provider("verification")
```

Create a session with `verification.create_verification_session(user, 'document', options={...})`. `user` is an application object with `id` (and optionally `username`); `options` may contain `return_url`, `email`, and `metadata`. The method returns a normalized session dictionary. Other operations retrieve/list/cancel/redact sessions and inspect verification status/reports. Listing returns the provider's dictionary envelope with `data` objects.

`handle_webhook(payload, signature)` needs the endpoint signing secret and raises `IdentityVerificationError` without one: set `verification.stripe_webhook_secret` (environment `SWAPLAYER_VERIFICATION_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), pass `webhook_secret` to the provider constructor, or keep the legacy Django `STRIPE_IDENTITY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` setting. Verify signatures against raw request bytes, then authorize and apply state changes in your application. Never trust a client redirect as proof of completed verification.

Use Stripe test mode and follow Stripe's current retention and production requirements. The library does not certify a person, decide compliance obligations, or implement an application's identity access policy. Redaction is a provider operation and needs explicit application authorization.

Optional Django model/admin mixins are under `swap_layer.identity.verification.models` and `.admin`. Applications own concrete models, migrations, access restrictions and retention. Runtime MCP tools provide guidance, not live production verification calls.
explain.mcp:
# MCP server

`swaplayer-mcp` is SwapLayer's local stdio MCP server. `pip install SwapLayer` installs it, and it needs no MCP SDK. `python -m swap_layer.mcp` starts the same server, and so does `python mcp/server.py` from a source checkout. Package and server version are 1.0.0.

This is a local process controlled by its caller. There is no hosted MCP endpoint, shared provider credential, paid agent account, or owner token supplied by the package. GitHub issues, public PRs and comments cannot authorize repository jobs or the owner's agents.

## Configuration

The server reads the caller's `SWAPLAYER_` environment configuration. For example:

```bash
# PowerShell: set $env:SWAPLAYER_STORAGE_PROVIDER = "local" instead of export.
export SWAPLAYER_STORAGE_PROVIDER=local
export SWAPLAYER_STORAGE_MEDIA_ROOT=./media
swaplayer-mcp
```

Every settings field has an environment path, identity and verification included (for example `SWAPLAYER_IDENTITY_WORKOS_APPS_DEFAULT_API_KEY`, `SWAPLAYER_VERIFICATION_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `SWAPLAYER_RAISE_ON_ERROR`), and a misspelt `SWAPLAYER_` variable fails validation. The command does not read `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`. Programmatic callers may instead configure SwapLayer (`swap_layer.configure(...)`, or Django settings after `django.setup()`) before calling `main()` or `create_mcp_server()`. Provider extras such as `SwapLayer[stripe]` are separate. [`mcp-config-example.json`](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/mcp-config-example.json) and [`examples/vscode-mcp.json`](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/examples/vscode-mcp.json) show client settings, the second in VS Code's `servers` format.

## Contract, resources and prompts

The server serves the packaged public agent contract (`swap_layer/mcp/agent-contract.json`) as `swap-layer-public-contract-mcp`. Its resources are under `opensource://swap_layer/`: `agent-contract`, `overview`, `public-apis`, `workflows`, `browser-surfaces`, `security-and-audit`, and `docs/<topic>` for the 11 packaged guides. Its prompts are `agent_onboarding`, `onboard_service`, `choose_provider` and `migrate_provider`, with snake_case arguments such as `user_goal` and `from_provider`. It validates JSON-RPC input, limits message size, and recovers after malformed input. The repository URL is documentation, not a hosted agent endpoint.

## Tools

Tool arguments are camelCase, and the services are `billing`, `email`, `sms`, `storage`, `identity` and `verification`.

| Tool | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `describe_offering` | SwapLayer, its service families, and the safe operating model |
| `list_public_capabilities` | Package APIs, docs, CLI commands, and these tools |
| `map_workflow_to_tools` | Tools, Python APIs, docs, approvals and verification for a goal |
| `operate_browser_docs` | Guidance for public docs, PyPI, GitHub issues or provider docs in a browser |
| `prepare_provider_setup` | Install command, settings template, environment placeholders and provider notes (`service`, `provider`, `projectType`) |
| `plan_provider_migration` | Migration checklist between two providers that touches no data (`fromProvider`, `toProvider`) |
| `explain` | One packaged guide (`topic`) |
| `compare_providers` | Provider comparison for a service, with an optional `useCase` |
| `troubleshoot` | A known setup problem; `errorMessage` is matched to symptoms and never returned |
| `list_providers` | Provider values the factory accepts |
| `get_provider_info` | One provider's capabilities, settings example and install command |
| `generate_code` | A Python example; returns text without executing it |
| `get_usage_examples` | Usage patterns for a service |
| `get_config` | The caller's configuration, public fields only |
| `send_test_email` | Sends one email using the caller's provider account |
| `send_test_sms` | Sends one SMS using the caller's provider account |
| `check_storage` | Storage configuration check; `testUpload: true` writes, then deletes, one file under `swaplayer-mcp-check/` |

`explain` topics are `overview` (the README), `docs-index`, `architecture`, `billing`, `email`, `sms`, `storage`, `identity-platform`, `identity-verification`, `mcp`, `security` (SECURITY.md), `philosophy` and `faq`.

Clients must obtain explicit approval before test sends or writes. They can incur charges or modify caller infrastructure. A label saying "test" does not switch provider credentials into sandbox mode. Configure a test account and approved recipient yourself. Do not expose this stdio process as an unauthenticated network service.

`get_config` returns only public settings fields (providers, options and public IDs), never credentials, and `swaplayer_check --verbose` masks every other value; operational errors omit raw exception messages. This is not a universal secret scanner for arbitrary user text, SDK logging or application data. Do not paste credentials into tool arguments. Application production transactions use the Python adapters behind application authorization, not autonomous documentation tools.

## Embedding

`swap_layer.mcp.create_mcp_server()` builds an MCP SDK server with the same contract, tools and prompts, to run inside your own process. It needs `SwapLayer[mcp]` (MCP Python SDK 1.x).

Third-party client settings determine model access and approval behavior. Configure the client to approve sensitive operations; repository and package policies do not grant that approval on your behalf.
explain.security:
# Security policy

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported          |
| ------- | ------------------ |
| 1.0.x   | :white_check_mark: |
| < 1.0   | :x:                |

Security fixes ship as new 1.0.x releases on
[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/SwapLayer/). SwapLayer 1.0.0 is tagged (`v1.0.0`)
but not yet published there; PyPI still serves 0.3.0, and versions below 1.0
are not supported.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not report a suspected vulnerability in a public issue, pull request, or
discussion. Report it privately in either of these ways:

- On GitHub, open the repository's **Security** tab and choose
  **Report a vulnerability**
  ([direct link](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/security/advisories/new)).
- Email **alex@tunet.xyz**.

Include a description, the affected versions, reproduction steps, the potential
impact, and any suggested mitigation. Use synthetic examples; do not send
credentials, personal data, or production samples.

## Response targets

We aim to acknowledge reports within 48 hours and provide an initial assessment
within five business days. Targets begin when severity is confirmed:

| Severity | Containment/mitigation target | Fix target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | 24 hours | 7 days |
| High | 3 business days | 14 days |
| Moderate | 10 business days | 30 days |
| Low | 30 days | 90 days |

These are maximum targets, not a promise to delay urgent fixes. If a complete
fix needs longer, we will prioritize a safe mitigation, coordinate disclosure,
and communicate a revised timeline privately. Please allow a reasonable period
for remediation before public disclosure. We will request a CVE and publish a
GitHub security advisory when impact warrants it.

## Scope

### In scope

- Storage keys or tenant scopes that escape the configured root or
  organization prefix, through traversal, absolute paths, symlinks, or
  junctions.
- Provider credentials exposed through MCP output, diagnostics, exception
  messages, or logs.
- Webhook signature verification that accepts an unsigned or forged event.
- Auth0 or WorkOS sessions or token caches shared across tenants or
  applications.
- Provider HTTP calls that can hang without a timeout.
- MCP tools marked read-only that send messages, write files, or change
  provider state.

### Out of scope

- Vulnerabilities in provider services or SDKs (Stripe, PayPal, Square,
  Twilio, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, WorkOS, and Auth0); report them to the
  provider.
- Vulnerabilities in Django or other dependencies; report them to those
  projects.
- Provider account, credential, and webhook endpoint configuration, which the
  application owns.
- Issues that require physical access to the server.

## Secure use

- Keep provider secrets in environment variables or a secret manager, never in
  source control, and rotate provider API keys regularly.
- Use HTTPS in production, verify provider webhook signatures, and give WorkOS
  a Fernet key as its cookie password.
- For tenant isolation, use `StorageSecurityContext` with an explicit
  `scope_format` through `storage_context()` or `ScopedStorageProvider`.
  Contexts trust identity your application has already verified. With several
  WorkOS or Auth0 apps, keep each tenant's app configuration separate.
- Keep local storage roots and their parents writable only by trusted
  application processes. Path checks do not replace a filesystem sandbox
  against concurrent replacement, and local URLs are unsigned, so control
  access to private files in your application.
- Store sealed WorkOS sessions securely in Django sessions.
- The MCP tools run locally with your own credentials. Test sends and storage
  probes can cause provider charges or file changes, so approve each such call;
  none of the owner's agents, accounts, or tokens is involved.

The [threat model](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md),
[security assurance case](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_ASSURANCE.md),
[audit scope](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/AUDIT_SCOPE.md), and
[secure development](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/SECURE_DEVELOPMENT.md) documents describe the design
assumptions, evidence, and residual risks in more detail.

## Releases and advisories

Security fixes are released from a reviewed commit on `main` through the
owner-approved trusted-publishing workflow described in
[docs/RELEASE.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md). Workflows run only when the owner starts
them, and PyPI uploads use short-lived OIDC credentials from a protected
environment. Stable API changes follow [VERSIONING.md](https://github.com/Tunet-xyz/swap_layer/blob/main/VERSIONING.md); a
security fix may intentionally reject previously accepted ambiguous input, with
the compatibility and migration impact explained in the release notes. Pin and
verify release artifacts, watch this repository's security advisories, test
your integration, and upgrade supported versions promptly.

missing_config.cause: The SWAPLAYER setting is not defined in Django settings.py
missing_config.solution: Call swap_layer.configure(...) in plain Python, or configure Django SWAPLAYER with billing, communications, storage, identity or verification groups. Use prepare_provider_setup for a valid example.

missing_package.cause: The provider's SDK package is not installed
missing_package.solution:
Install the appropriate SwapLayer extra for your provider:

| Provider | Command |
|----------|---------|
| Stripe | `pip install "SwapLayer[stripe]"` |
| SendGrid / Mailgun / SES | `pip install "SwapLayer[email]"` |
| Twilio | `pip install "SwapLayer[sms]"` |
| AWS (SNS, S3) | `pip install "SwapLayer[aws]"` |
| Azure Blob | `pip install "SwapLayer[azure]"` |
| WorkOS / Auth0 | `pip install "SwapLayer[identity]"` |
| MCP server | `pip install "SwapLayer[mcp]"` |

Or install everything: `pip install "SwapLayer[all]"`

invalid_credentials.cause: API key, token, or credentials are wrong or expired
invalid_credentials.solution:
Check your credentials:

1. Verify environment variables are set:
```bash
echo $STRIPE_SECRET_KEY   # should start with sk_
echo $SENDGRID_API_KEY    # should start with SG.
echo $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID  # should start with AC
```

2. For Stripe: use test keys (sk_test_...) in development, live keys (sk_live_...) in production.

3. Confirm the key has the correct permissions in the provider dashboard.

4. Check for leading/trailing whitespace in environment variables.

5. Verify the key isn't expired or revoked in the provider dashboard.

wrong_provider_name.cause: Provider name in configuration doesn't match an available provider
wrong_provider_name.solution: Provider values are lowercase. Email selects django/smtp; SendGrid and Mailgun use the Django Anymail backend. Storage selects local/django/gcs; S3/Azure use Django STORAGES. Verification selects stripe.

django_not_setup.cause: Django application registry isn't initialized before SwapLayer is used
django_not_setup.solution:
Ensure Django is set up before using SwapLayer:

```python
import os
import django

os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'myproject.settings')
django.setup()  # must be called before get_provider()

from swap_layer import get_provider
email = get_provider('email')
```

In management commands or scripts, Django is set up automatically.
In tests, use `@pytest.mark.django_db` or configure pytest-django.

mcp_not_installed.cause: The mcp package is not installed
mcp_not_installed.solution:
Install the MCP extra:

```bash
pip install "SwapLayer[mcp]"
```

Then run the MCP server:
```bash
swaplayer-mcp
```

Or run directly:
```bash
python -m swap_layer.mcp
```
